title: Stanley Dance coaxes her into the Carnegie Hall Basie tribute
summary: Dance turns to the 1972 comeback. Stanley Dance visited Louisville and urged her to sing in a Newport tribute to Basie at Carnegie Hall. She doubted herself, Nellie Lutcher calmed her backstage, and she was sensational.

blocks.x: Well listen Helen, I think the time has come and get started now and think about what happened after you had gone home, which we talked about earlier, and you were taking care of your dad and it was about 1973, and Stanley Dance.
Stanley Dance, he called up and he said, 'Helen can I come out?' I said, 'alright'. I went over and picked him up.
And drove him on out. And then he started talking about wanting me to come and do this Basie.
Yeah. Well this was a tribute to Armstrong. Oh no, this was the Basie one.

And I said, "oh my goodness I haven't even hummed since I've been home. I can't do nothing". He said, "yes you can Helen. Now you can sing." I said, "well it's been so long I don't know whether I can sing or not". He said, "well why don't you come on and try". I said, "because Carnegie Hall is too big to be trying to sing in". And so he said, "well, just come on, you can make it". And I said, "well, alright then, if you think I can make I'll come on and sing something". So I went on and Nellie Lutcher, bless her heart, she came and she said, "Helen I'll stay right here with you until you go on". She said, "don't be scared". And I said, "well you know every time I get nervous and I get hoarse and everything". She ran across the street to the drug store and she brought me more cough drops and cough syrups and stuff. And I said, "well if I ain't feeling better now, I won't". And I went on and it was sensational.
